question: A train of length 384 metres crosses an electric pole in 12 seconds and crosses another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
solution:
**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ Length of the train (L) = 384 meters

⇒ Time to cross a pole (T₁) = 12 seconds

Speed of the first train (V₁):

⇒ V₁ = L / T₁ = 384 meters / 12 seconds = 32 m/s

Time to cross the second train (T₂) = 12 seconds

Relative speed of both
 trains when traveling in opposite directions (V₁ + V₂):

⇒ Total distance covered = Length of first train + Length of second train

⇒ Total distance = 384 meters + 384 meters = 768 meters

⇒ Relative speed = Total distance / T₂ = 768/12 = 64 m/s

Since V₁ = 32 m/s, we have:

⇒ V₁ + V₂ = 64 m/s

⇒ 32 m/s + V₂ = 64 m/s

⇒ V₂ = 64 m/s - 32 m/s = 32 m/s

**∴ The speed of the second train is 32 m/s, hence the correct answer is option 4.**
